extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/agents preparing patent applications and Information Disclosure Statements (IDSs)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/formatting requirements from the MPEP governing computer program listings, large tables, sequence listings, and Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) — including timing, content, electronic submission, and examiner handling. Applies to preparing and examining filing materials to ensure compliance with 37 CFR and USPTO practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listing length and placement (>60 and ≤300 lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer program listing of over sixty (60) lines and less than three hundred and one (301) lines must, if submitted as part of the specification, be positioned at the end of the specification and before the claims, in accordance with 37 CFR 1.96(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is required to cancel the paper listing and either incorporate the listing in a text file submitted via EFS‑Web or on compact disc in compliance with 37 CFR 1.96, or insert the computer program listing after the detailed description but before the claims. Use the specified form paragraph whenever a paper printout of >60 and ≤300 lines is included and was filed on/after September 8, 2000. A computer program listing of more than three hundred lines will not be printed in any patent application publication or patent (37 CFR 1.96(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listing appendix identification and specification statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Computer Program Listing Appendix submitted electronically via EFS‑Web in ASCII text or on compact disc will be identified as such in the patent but will not be part of the printed patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement must be included in the specification that a computer program listing appendix on compact disc is included in the application. The specification entry should appear at the beginning of the specification following any cross‑reference to related applications (37 CFR 1.77(b)(5)). When compact discs are received by OPAP an artifact folder will be created and the application will proceed normally. Historical microfiche practice continued only until March 1, 2001; pre‑March‑2‑2001 microfiche in conformance with former rules may rely on microfiche.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microfiche appendix unacceptable after cutoff
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'microfiche appendix' filed after March 1, 2001, or a microfiche appendix filed on/before March 1, 2001 that is not in compliance with the former rule, is unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 6.64.04 to notify applicant that a microfiche appendix is unacceptable and that a computer program listing conforming to 37 CFR 1.96 is required. Insert the date the microfiche appendix was filed where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission of large tables must preserve spatial relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables submitted in electronic form (§§ 1.96(c) and 1.821(c)) must maintain the spatial relationships (e.g., alignment of columns and rows) of the table elements when displayed so as to visually preserve the relational information they convey; chemical and mathematical formulae must be encoded to maintain proper positioning of characters (37 CFR 1.58).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting tables electronically, ensure the spatial arrangement of data in rows and columns is maintained so the table can be viewed with virtually any text viewer. No special formatting characters or proprietary formats are permitted for ASCII submissions. Misalignment that prevents accurate reading will require applicant to submit a replacement text file via EFS‑Web or compact disc with proper alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASCII text file requirements for tables and listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Text files submitted via EFS‑Web or on compact disc containing tables or listings must contain only ASCII characters; no special formatting characters or proprietary file formats are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great care must be taken so that spatial arrangement of the data in rows and columns is maintained when the file is opened at the Office. This allows the table to be viewed with virtually any text viewer. A single table ≤50 pages has different submission options (see related criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thresholds for submitting tables on paper/PDF vs. compact disc/ASCII via EFS‑Web
rubrics_metrics.description: A single table contained on fifty (50) pages or less must be submitted either as drawings (37 CFR 1.84) or as part of the specification in paper (37 CFR 1.52) or PDF (if filed via EFS‑Web). A single table of 51 pages or more, or multiple tables whose total pages exceed 100, may be submitted on CD‑ROM/CD‑R (37 CFR 1.52(e) and 1.58) or as an ASCII text file via EFS‑Web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'table page' is defined per 37 CFR 1.52(e)(1)(iii) as a page printed on paper conforming to 37 CFR 1.52(b) and 1.58(c). Do not subdivide a large table with subheadings into sections simply to avoid CD submission unless subdivided tables are presented as numerous files on CD without losing relationship to the overall table. If submitted as CD or text file, lengthy tables may be handled differently (see 'lengthy tables' criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on subdividing headings to avoid CD submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of a subheading to divide a large table into smaller sections of less than 51 pages should not be used to prevent submission on compact disc unless the subdivided tables are presented as numerous files on the compact disc so as to lose their relationship to the overall large table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may require submission on compact disc or ASCII if subdivision appears intended to evade submission rules. Maintain the logical relationship of table data when subdividing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landscape orientation identification for CD submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables in landscape orientation should be identified as landscape orientation in the transmittal letter accompanying the compact disc to allow the Office to properly upload the tables into Image File Wrapper (IFW) or other automated systems (37 CFR 1.52(e)(3)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most tables are intended to render in portrait mode. Filings without an identification of landscape will be rendered as portrait mode by the Office. Landscape oriented tables should not be filed via EFS‑Web because PAIR will automatically convert to portrait orientation and may distort images during viewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lengthy tables publication policy and 'LENGTHY TABLE' placeholder
rubrics_metrics.description: If tables on more than two hundred consecutive pages, or large numbers of tables (lengthy tables), are submitted on CD or via EFS‑Web, these lengthy tables will not be published as part of a patent document; they will be published separately on the USPTO website (e.g., seqdata.uspto.gov) as an XML file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office discourages embedding a lengthy table in the specification. If embedded but available electronically, a single‑column 'LENGTHY TABLE' statement will be inserted in the patent document in place of each replaced table with directions to access the table at the end of the specification or on the USPTO website. Standardized page‑wide text for patent, patent application publication, or SIR is provided; include page range references as indicated in form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement when table column/row relationship not maintained
rubrics_metrics.description: If a table submitted as an ASCII text file does not maintain the data within each table cell in its proper row/column alignment, the applicant is required to submit a replacement text file via EFS‑Web or on compact disc with the table data properly aligned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the form paragraph that explains the specific area of the table that does not maintain alignment and require replacement. This form paragraph is used whenever data in a table cannot be accurately read due to misalignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table less than 51 pages submitted only as text file is noncompliant
rubrics_metrics.description: A table consisting of less than fifty‑one (51) pages submitted only in ASCII text format via EFS‑Web or on compact disc (as part of the descriptive portion) does not comply with 37 CFR 1.52(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must cancel references to the table in text format appearing in the specification, file a paper version of the table in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52 or file a PDF via EFS‑Web, and change all appropriate references to the former text version throughout the specification. Use the designated form paragraph for notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing biological sequence listings as ASCII files allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of biological sequence information on compact disc or in text format via EFS‑Web is permitted in lieu of filing on paper (see MPEP § 608.05 and § 2422.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 502.05 and the EFS‑Web Legal Framework for submissions via EFS‑Web. Follow the sequence listing submission rules and formats described in the referenced MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS considered only if filed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.97 timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) will be considered by the Office if filed by the applicant within the time periods specified in 37 CFR 1.97 (e.g., within three months of the filing date of a national application other than a CPA, or within three months of national stage entry, or before the mailing of a first Office action on the merits, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.97 lists multiple timing windows: (b)(1) within three months of filing or before first OA (national apps), (b)(2) within three months of national stage entry, (b)(3) before first OA on the merits, (b)(4) before the first OA after filing a request for continued examination, (b)(5) within three months of publication for certain design apps. IDS filed after these windows may be considered if accompanied by required statements or fees per 1.97(c)/(d), but IDS filed after payment of the issue fee will not be considered. No extensions of time under 1.136 are permitted for IDS filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for IDS listings (format and per‑item identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any IDS must include the items listed in 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1)–(3): a list of all patents, publications, applications, or other information submitted; U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications must be listed separately; each page of the list must include the application number, a column for examiner initials, and a heading clearly indicating the list is an Information Disclosure Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper identification for each cited item is required: (i) U.S. patents by inventor, patent number, and issue date; (ii) U.S. patent application publications by applicant, publication number, and publication date; (iii) U.S. applications by inventor, application number, and filing date; (iv) foreign patents/publications by country/office, document number (including kind code), and publication/issue date; (v) non‑patent literature by publisher, author (if any), title, relevant pages, date, and place of publication. Include the fee set forth in 1.17(p) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies required with IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS must be accompanied by legible copies as specified in 37 CFR 1.98(a): for each cited foreign patent document, each cited non‑patent literature or relevant portion, each cited U.S. pending application not stored in IFW, all information cited (e.g., affidavit or Office action) other than the specification, and all other cited information or portions which caused listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disclosures of two or more patents/publications are substantively cumulative, a copy of one may be submitted without copies of the other(s) provided it is stated that the others are cumulative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑English documents in an IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: For non‑English documents cited in an IDS, a concise explanation of the relevance of each such document is required as presently understood by the individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) most knowledgeable about the content, unless a complete English translation is provided (37 CFR 1.98).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The concise explanation may be separate from the specification or incorporated therein. If a written English translation is within the possession, custody, or control of, or is readily available to, any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c), a copy of the translation should be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and format requirements for IDS (37 CFR 1.33(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To have an IDS considered, it must meet content requirements of 37 CFR 1.98, be filed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.97, and be signed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.33(b) (e.g., a separate signed page referencing and accompanying the IDS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An e‑IDS submission via EFS‑Web in compliance with the EFS‑Web framework satisfies the signature requirement. If the minimum requirements are met, the examiner must consider the information. Information failing to meet 1.97/1.98/1.33(b) will be placed in the file but not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing an IDS (no implied search or admission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an IDS shall not be construed as a representation that a search has been made, nor as an admission that the information cited is material to patentability as defined in 37 CFR 1.56(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no requirement that applicant make a patentability search. The IDS mechanism provides a uniform way to submit information to be considered by the Office; admissions by applicant are discussed separately (MPEP § 2129).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party submissions and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties (individuals not covered by 37 CFR 1.56(c)) cannot file IDSs under 37 CFR 1.97/1.98. Third parties may submit patents and publications in compliance with 37 CFR 1.290 in applications published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b); for unpublished pending applications third parties may file a protest under 37 CFR 1.291 prior to mailing of a notice of allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties may provide information to the applicant to allow the applicant to submit it in an IDS (see 37 CFR 1.56(d)). Any third‑party submission not in compliance with 1.290/1.291 will not be entered into the application file and will be discarded. Office personnel are instructed not to reply to or act upon third‑party inquiries or submissions except as authorized by 1.290/1.291, and to decline oral/telephone comments from third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner consideration and marking of IDS citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Once minimum requirements of 37 CFR 1.97, 1.98, and 1.33(b) are met, the examiner must consider the information submitted in the IDS in the same manner as other documents in Office search files while conducting a search in a proper field of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should indicate consideration by initialing the blank column next to each citation or by using an alternative electronic signature method: inserting on each page the phrase 'All references considered except where lined through' with electronic initials and the examiner’s electronic signature on the final page. Examiners will no longer initial each reference; they will strikethrough citations not considered and stamp each page 'All references considered except where lined through' with electronic initials. Information not complying with requirements will be placed in the file but not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner checklist: time‑related IDS checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must check whether an IDS complies with all time‑related requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 (different requirements depending on national app, national stage, RCE/CPA, international design apps, and post‑filing windows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MPEP § 609.04(b) for more detail. The checklist enumerates scenarios and the required accompanying statements/fees when IDSs are filed outside the initial windows (e.g., 1.97(e) statement and/or 1.17(p) fee). If IDS filed after payment of issue fee it will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner checklist: content checks for IDS listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must check that IDS content requirements per 37 CFR 1.98 are met: separate US patent/publication section; application number on each page if known; a column for examiner initials; clear heading identifying listing as an IDS; proper identification of cited references; copies provided for required items; and non‑English document handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific subitems: (a) separate section for U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications; (b) application number on each page; (c) blank space next to each document for examiner initials; (d) proper identification formats for U.S. patents/publications/pending apps/foreign docs/non‑patent literature; (e) copies required for foreign docs, non‑patent literature, pending U.S. apps not in IFW, and other cited materials. See MPEP § 609.04(a) for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner actions after IDS compliance review
rubrics_metrics.description: After reviewing an IDS for compliance with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98, the examiner should consider properly submitted information, indicate consideration using initials or the electronic method, draw a line through citations that fail to comply, inform applicant why a citation was not considered, sign and date the IDS listing (or use electronic method), and ensure the signed copy is entered into the file and mailed to applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of the information complies, write 'not considered' on the IDS and notify applicant using form paragraphs 6.49–6.49.10. Ensure the examiner’s signature/date or electronic signature is present on the IDS listing and that a copy is placed in the file and mailed to applicant. For e‑IDS, use the e‑IDS icon on examiner’s workstation to consider cited U.S. patents and publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple IDSs and use of PTO/SB/08A and 08B forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple IDSs may be filed in a single application and will be considered provided each complies with 37 CFR 1.97, 1.98, and 1.33(b). Use of PTO/SB/08A and 08B forms is encouraged to provide the required listing format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTO/SB/08A and 08B are updated by the Office and enable applicants to comply with listing requirements and provide a uniform listing that makes it easy for the examiner to indicate consideration. If resubmitting listings in a continuing application avoid submitting completed PTO/SB/08 forms from other applications (they may contain prior examiner initials and other application identifiers that cause confusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS practice in continuing/prosecution applications (CPAs, continuations, divisional, CIPs, RCEs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information that has been considered by the Office in a parent application of a continuing application (including CPAs filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d), continuations, divisionals, CIPs, and prior to filing an RCE) will be part of the file before the examiner and generally need not be resubmitted in the continuing application to have the information considered and listed on the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If resubmitting a listing, applicant should submit a new listing that complies with 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1) and the timing requirements of 37 CFR 1.97. Applicants are strongly discouraged from submitting lists that include copies of PTO/SB/08 or PTO‑892 forms from other applications because prior initials and application numbers may confuse the record. Specific rules apply for international‑origin documents and national‑stage situations; see MPEP § 609.03 and related subsections.
